oldehove.name: Oldehove
oldehove.slogan: Leeuwarden's tower leans two metres and still stands tall.
oldehove.line: Work began in 1529 and stopped in 1532 because the tower had already started to tilt; its top sits about 2 metres off centre.

planetarium.name: Eise Eisinga Planetarium
planetarium.slogan: A wool comber put the whole sky on his living-room ceiling.
planetarium.line: Eise Eisinga built it from 1774 to 1781; its gears use about 10,000 handmade nails and it is the oldest working planetarium in the world.

woudagemaal.name: Woudagemaal
woudagemaal.slogan: Steam still keeps Friesland's feet dry, in a brick cathedral of pumps.
woudagemaal.line: Opened by Queen Wilhelmina on 7 October 1920, it is the largest steam pumping station still working and a UNESCO site since 1998.

princessehof.name: Princessehof Ceramics Museum
princessehof.slogan: A regent's tile collection, in the house where Escher was born.
princessehof.line: M.C. Escher was born in 1898 in one of the houses that now form the museum, whose ceramics span 2800 BC to the 20th century.

hindeloopen.name: Hindeloopen
hindeloopen.slogan: Sea captains' wives painted a whole town in roses and blue.
hindeloopen.line: Hindeloopen got city rights in 1225 and today has under 900 residents, famous for its painted walls and furniture.
